<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Sanders** · [Slack thread](https://electronhq.slack.com/archives/C0BD3CT26G6/p1786034336896949?thread_ts=1786034336.896949&cid=C0BD3CT26G6)_

**Before:** running `npm install` on a 32-bit Node.js fails with a cryptic `ENOENT` about `vendor\7z-ia32.exe`, or installer creation fails obscurely partway through packaging.

**After:** `createWindowsInstaller` throws `32-bit build machines are not supported` before attempting any work, and the install script prints a clear warning instead of crashing.

**How:**
- `createWindowsInstaller` now calls a new exported `assertSupportedArch()` helper (unit-tested) that throws on non-x64/arm64 host architectures.
- `script/select-7z-arch.js` prints a one-line warning and exits 0 on unsupported architectures instead of crashing with `ENOENT`, and now calls `os.arch()` properly (it previously read the function reference without invoking it).
- The README gains a "Supported platforms" section explaining that x64/arm64 build machines are required, and that apps targeting 32-bit Windows (Electron <= 43) can still be packaged from a 64-bit machine.

Fixes #612
Fixes #386
Fixes #474
Fixes #558

comments.body:
Hello @dsanders11 

However, `os.arch()` returns `"ia32"` on an x64 machine when running a 32-bit Node.js binary (since we're building a 32-bit app from an x64 machine, as mentioned in this PR). According to the Node.js documentation, `os.arch()` returns the CPU architecture for which the Node.js binary was compiled, not necessarily the architecture of the underlying operating system.

_Working with **Erick Zhao**_

You're right about the mechanics: `os.arch()` reports the architecture the Node.js binary was compiled for, not the OS's. That's the intended check here, though. The 7-Zip binary this package uses is selected by the Node.js process's architecture, and only x64 and arm64 binaries are bundled — so a 32-bit Node.js process is the unsupported configuration, regardless of the OS underneath. That's why the error and README say to switch to 64-bit Node.js if you're on 64-bit Windows.

Packaging a 32-bit (ia32) Electron app (Electron <= 43) still works from 64-bit Node.js, and the generated installer runs on 32-bit Windows — only the build-machine Node.js needs to be 64-bit.
